51196081.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to human p38alpha expressed in Escherichia coli by surface plasmon resonance analysis
51196081.references_previous: 15. Karlsson, R.; Stahlberg, R. Anal. Biochem. 1995, 228, 274.

original_paragraph.SPR Analysis: Surface Plasmon Resonance (SPR) technology was used to obtain comparative direct binding data for both compounds on immobilized unphosphorylated p38α and p38β protein (Table 3).15 Based on the measured net association rates (ka) and dissociation rates (kd), KD values were determined using the formula kd/ka = KD for each compound. Using this data, 3 and 5q were calculated to have α/β selectivities of ~2- and 120-fold, respectively, which are in close agreement to their corresponding α/β selectivities determined from the enzyme inhibition assays. These results confirm that 5q is at least 50-fold more selective for p38α over β relative to 3 and provide further confirmation of the credibility of the high α/β selectivities observed within this new series. Furthermore, these data also confirm that the higher observed α/β selectivities are largely a result of decreased potency toward inhibiting p38β. The SPR data demonstrate significantly faster dissociation rates for each compound with the β-isofrom, relative to the α-isofrom. For the more selective 5q, in addition to >10-fold faster dissociation rate for the β-isofrom, the net association rate is also ~5-fold slower. These factors combine to yield the observed >100-fold α/β selectivity. A faster dissociation rate corresponds to a shorter residence time of 5q on the surface of the β-isofrom, and is indicative of a less optimal interaction with the β-active site. Possible structural features relevant to this observation are discussed below.
